name: Communism
summary: Communism aims at a classless society in which the means of production are held in common, money and wage labour disappear, and goods are distributed according to need. Following Marx and Engels, it sees history as driven by class struggle and holds that capitalism must be overthrown by a working-class revolution. In its Marxist-Leninist form a vanguard party leads a transitional dictatorship of the proletariat that nationalises and plans the economy before the state is expected to wither away.
scope: Marxist communism in the lineage of Marx and Engels (Communist Manifesto, Critique of the Gotha Programme) as developed by Lenin (The State and Revolution) into Marxism-Leninism, the doctrine of the ruling communist parties at the movement's 20th-century peak. Where communist parties differ on current social questions, answers follow the classic texts and mark the split. It excludes anarcho-communism, left communism and council communism (which reject the party-state) and post-1978 Chinese market reforms.
